entries.title: Jeremiah 47:1
segments:
Before that Pharaoh smote Gaza; this is mentioned simply as a date; or the prophecy relates to the desolation of Philistia, not by Pharaoh, but by Nebuchadnezzar. 
 
God's judgments upon wicked nations often come like an overflowing flood which nothing can resist, and which sweeps away every thing. Before them the great and the mighty find themselves utterly helpless, having no power either to resist or to escape.  How terrible will be that great day of judgment which shall destroy for ever "all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch."

entries.title: Jeremiah 47:2
segments:
Waters; a symbol of overflowing and desolating armies. 
 
  Out of the north; out of Babylon.
It was during this expedition that his armies overran Philistia.  Compare

entries.title: Jeremiah 47:3
segments:
The fathers shall not look back to their children; shall not concern themselves about their safety. 
 
  Feebleness of hands; the effect of extreme terror.

entries.title: Jeremiah 47:4
segments: From Tyrua and Zidon; see note on

  Every helper that remaineth; every one who could help them against the common invader. 
 
  Caphtor; the original country of the Philistines: according to some, Cappadocia; according to others, the island of Crete.
